title: How Shayne Coplan Made Polymarket a Media Story
description: Polymarket found a way to remain relevant to news taking place beyond the crypto industry. Behind that is Shayne Coplan, who founded the company in 2020.
seoTitle: How Shayne Coplan Made Polymarket a Media Story
html:
In January 2026, Polymarket announced a partnership with Dow Jones that would bring its prediction market data to The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch and Investor's Business Daily.

 For a company that began as a crypto-based prediction platform, appearing inside some of the world's most established financial publications was a remarkable development. 

 Behind that growth is Shayne Coplan, who founded Polymarket in 2020. His company attracted widespread attention during the 2024 US presidential election, when its market probabilities became a recurring reference point in discussions about the race. But the more interesting marketing story is what happened after the election. 

 Polymarket found a way to remain relevant to conversations taking place far beyond the crypto industry. Its markets cover politics, economics, sports and entertainment, giving journalists a continuously updated source of information about how traders assess the likelihood of future events. A political development, an earnings announcement or a major sporting event can become another reason for people to encounter the platform. 

 This creates an unusual relationship between product and publicity. Media coverage introduces audiences to Polymarket, while Polymarket's data gives publishers material they can incorporate into their own reporting. The Dow Jones agreement formalised part of that relationship, turning the platform's core functionality into something that could be distributed through established media channels. There are limits to the model. Prediction market prices are not the same as public opinion, and questions about market manipulation, regulation and the reliability of trading signals remain important. Media visibility also brings greater scrutiny. 

 For marketers working in fintech and Web3, the case offers an interesting lesson in positioning. Polymarket became relevant to audiences that might never have actively searched for a crypto product because its information connected with subjects they already followed. The question worth asking is whether your product has something valuable enough for other people to discuss, reference or incorporate into their own work.
